commands.name: pair
commands.description: Issue a pairing code for a new device on another machine: 16 characters, valid ten minutes, for one device and five attempts. Entered there with 'vericairn connections add', it records the device with the key it presents and admits it under your authority (needs the runtime serving the local-network profile).

commands.name: presence
commands.description: From 0.9.4: choose, on the machine holding a person's device key, whether its signatures ask one presence check per signature or one per operator action's announced list (a presence session), and the session's limit; kept owner-only in this user's machine state, never in a record. Without a choice it shows the device's setting. The estate's charter (policies.presence) may ask per-signature for every device, and the stricter of the two wins.

commands.name: recovery
commands.description: Make the operator's recovery device for emergency access: its key is written once to a file, encrypted with a passphrase you type, and never held by this machine; an admitted device of the operator held here admits it (record format 2).

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename a device whose key is held here; it keeps its identity, key and admission (record format 2).

commands.name: revoke
commands.description: Revoke a device's admission from now on; its earlier records stay attributable.

commands.name: rotate
commands.description: Replace a device's key with a new one, signed by both keys; the device keeps its identity and admission, and its earlier records stay valid (record format 2).

commands.name: sessions
commands.description: From 0.9.4: list the presence sessions this machine's runtime opened or tried to open for the estate, from its owner-only ledger: each session's action, device, fingerprint, when and why it opened and ended, the records signed under it by id and hash, and each refusal. The ledger is a diagnostic in this user's machine state, never a record, an export or a support bundle; no daemon is needed.

commands.name: writes
commands.description: List what paired devices wrote over the local network through this machine's runtime: when, which device, for which principal, the operation and the record it produced. A record a paired device asks for is signed by a device of the same principal held here, so this is where the paired device behind it is kept. From 0.9.2 it also lists network MCP writes on loopback, which their own device signed.

commands.description: Record a document's next revision. Converted documents regenerate their revision history and hash authored content; existing whole-file pins keep their mode. --convert-revisions converts the opening history. --render-template needs an estate template instance or a converted revision history, and refreshes it, also with unchanged authored bytes; a plain whole-file document has neither, and its summary is corrected with records new document-revision, as the living-documents guide shows.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Record a review of a living document: the runtime reads its content, records the covered paths' identity and the triggers it answers, and runs its declared checks; a failed check refuses the clearance. A reviewer who did not revise the content records current, whoever revised it: after a builder pins a revision, a separate reviewer clears those exact bytes with --outcome current.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Check this machine's prerequisites. With --json, writes one JSON object with the report's facts under stable names: version, runtime, git, dotnet, estate, custody, enclave, presence, records, search and daemon, each an object of state (present, missing, unavailable or not-applicable), value and detail, and stateWarnings, the per-user state whose permissions cannot be restricted. Discloses and checks GitHub for a newer published release at most once per 24 hours, shared with Workbench; no identifiers or usage telemetry. Disclosure and upgrade notices go to stderr, leaving stdout and JSON unchanged. Disable with vericairn updates configure --enabled false. Offline failures keep the cached answer and never fail this command.

commands.description: List the self-admissions that could be the estate's first authority, with the evidence for each, or name one of the root operator's own devices in the manifest's firstAuthority (0.9.3).
